name: Liftwise Labs
positioning: Liftwise puts sensors on workers to score how they lift; Keelstone sees the whole site through the cameras already on the wall, with nothing for workers to wear or charge. When the prospect wants coverage of every hazard, not only ergonomics, we win.

scorecard.note: Wearables give them more precise per-worker motion data.
Wearables avoid video, but track individuals by name.
Their haptic buzz coaches in the moment.
They report risk scores, not dollars.
Fast to ship devices, slow to get adoption.

whyWeWin.point: Nothing to wear, charge or lose
whyWeWin.proof: Runs on existing cameras; wearable programs commonly lose devices and adoption within months.
Slips, PPE, forklifts and lifts in one system.

whereTheyWin: Ergonomics-only buyers in warehousing and distribution
Sites with few cameras or poor sightlines
Customers who want individual worker scores

objections.youSay: For the workers who wear them. Ask what share were still wearing them at month six.

objections.theySay: No cameras means no privacy concerns.
objections.youSay: A device that scores each worker by name is personal data too. We never identify individuals by default.

landmines: Who charges and hands out the devices every shift?
What happens with temp and seasonal workers?
How will you see hazards that are not lifts?

products.name: Liftwise Clip
products.description: Wearable motion sensor with haptic coaching

products.name: Liftwise Insights
products.description: Ergonomic risk dashboard by worker and team

negative.detail: Workers stop wearing them; devices go missing.
Worries about the next funding round.
